definition: Yellowing of leaves due to insufficient chlorophyll production, often caused by disease, nutrient deficiency, or environmental stress.
Death of plant tissue, appearing as brown or black dead areas on leaves, stems, or fruit.
A localized area of diseased or damaged plant tissue, often discolored and irregularly shaped.
A pattern of light and dark green or yellow patches on leaves caused by viral infections.
An organism (typically insect) that transmits a pathogen from infected to healthy plants.
Pathogen material (spores, bacteria, virus particles) capable of causing infection in a susceptible host.
A fungicide or insecticide that is absorbed and transported throughout the plant, providing internal protection.
A fungicide that remains on the plant surface and protects against infection but does not enter plant tissue.
The removal and destruction of infected plants to prevent the spread of disease to healthy plants.
Disease management practices that modify the growing environment, such as crop rotation, sanitation, and irrigation management.
Use of natural enemies (predators, parasites, pathogens) to control pests and diseases.
A chemical compound used to control fungal diseases.
A chemical compound used to control insect pests.
The reproductive structure of a fungus that produces and releases spores.
The vegetative part of a fungus, consisting of a network of fine white filaments (hyphae).
